Hi Sarah / Luke —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the open discussion on product goals and expected usage patterns. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Primary feature set: conversational agent + summarization + search-augmentation (will drive most token volume).
- Expected volumes: baseline ~50M tokens/month, seasonal peak up to ~200M tokens/month (as you scale pilots).
- Latency & quality: sub-200ms token latency target for core chat flows; willing to consider model quantization if quality stays within SLAs.

Open pricing/volume items we discussed
- Target unit price: you mentioned wanting to land around $/1M tokens in the $600–$800 range (please confirm).
- Budget range: what procurement band should we be modeling for (annual committed spend OR monthly pay-as-you-go)?
- Unit economics asks: you asked for $/feature estimates, CAC payback examples, and margin vs inference cost — I’ve attached an initial pricing model and slide deck (RDW_pricing_model_v2.xlsx, unit_econ_slide_deck.pdf) that break down several scenarios.

Proposed next steps
1) Can you confirm: baseline vs peak token numbers and whether the pilot will have a fixed monthly spend or flexible? (This changes our recommended committed tiers.)
2) I’ll loop in Rishi (inference economics) and Marcus (solutions) to prepare a short unit-econ appendix for your finance team — aim to send by EOD 12/2.
3) If procurement is ready, propose a brief call with Luke + Mike + our legal/procurement on Dec 6 to align on contract timeline and SLA expectations.

If that all looks right, I’ll circulate the pricing scenarios and a short memo on CAC/payback examples for similar customers.

Thanks —

Marissa —

Attached is a completed draft of the inference-cost section (I updated RDW_pricing_model_v2.xlsx and added a short notes tab). High-level summary below; see sheet for the numbers and assumptions.

High-level inference cost scenarios (all $/1M tokens, gross infra cost to Redwood):
- Baseline (mixed FP16, no quantization, on-demand): ~$1,050 / 1M tokens
- Optimized (8-bit quant, continuous batching, reserved instances): ~$420 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated / committed (aggressive packing, KV cache reuse): ~$300 / 1M tokens

Suggested list price bands to achieve target gross margin (~50%):
- If customer target is $650 / 1M: marginally below our 50% margin on baseline but achievable with a mix of reserved capacity + some model/quantization work. Recommend contract morphology: 6–12 month commit with tiered discounts at 100M & 200M token bands.
- If customer targets $650–$800 / 1M: the $800 band yields ~55–60% gross margin under optimized configs; $650 is doable with committed volumes and cache/batching.

Per-feature examples (estimate of cost to Redwood, modeled as incremental token generation + average latency constraints):
- Smart-reply (avg output 20 tokens, high qps): ~ $0.0084 / feature (assuming 1M feature calls ~= 20M tokens)
- Full-convo (avg output 400 tokens across session with 800 context tokens): ~ $0.42 / feature (1M such sessions ~= 400M generated tokens + context cost)

CAC / payback illustrative example (simple):
- Assume LTV uplift = +$30 ARR per customer from assistant features; CAC for pilot cohort = $3,000; at price $650 / 1M tokens and average usage 60M tokens/mo per customer cohort, expected gross contribution allows payback in ~6–9 months depending on conversion lift. Full model in sheet.

Notes / asks for Marissa:
- Need confirmation on expected committed bands (monthly vs annual).
- If procurement requires $650 absolute cap, we should prioritize reserved capacity + quantization plan in SOW.

I attached the updated RDW_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (inference-cost tab) and a short notes doc. Happy to jump on a quick call with Sarah / Luke if they want the numbers walked through.

–Rishi
